1  IV ADDL.CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE,
 MAYOHALL UNIT: BENGALURU.
 JUDGMENT
The plaintiff has filed this suit against the defendant for ejectment, arrears of rent and damages.

2. In brief, the plaint averments are as under:-
The defendant is the tenant under plaintiff in respect of the shop premises as described in the schedule, under lease agreement dated 20.09.2017 for a period of two years on a monthly rentals at Rs.15,000/- from 01.04.2017 subject to enhancement at 10% on every 11 months.
The defendant has committed default in payment of rentals and as on 30.10.2020, he was liable to pay Rs.6,45,975/-.
After adjusting the security deposit of Rs.4 lakhs, the defendant is liable to pay arrears of rent Rs.2,45,975/-.
The plaintiff terminated the tenancy of the defendant by issuing a quit notice dated 10.11.2020, which was duly served upon the defendant.

Thereafter,
the defendant paid Rs.45,000/- which the plaintiff adjusted towards arrears of rent.

Hence, prayed to direct the defendant to deliver vacant possession of the suit property and to pay arrears of rent Rs.2,15,975/- with interest at 18% per Judgment annum and damages at Rs.50,000/- per month from the date of suit till the date of handing over vacant possession of the suit property.

3. The defendant has appeared and filed written statement, which he amended subsequently, in brief is as under:-
He admitted that he is a tenant under the plaintiff in respect of the suit property under the lease agreement, on security deposit of Rs.4 lakhs and monthly rentals at Rs.15,000/- per month.

He has carried out repairs of the suit property and built one more floor on top at his cost by spending Rs.2,50,000/-, which the plaintiff assured to return back while delivering vacant possession of the premises.
Earlier he filed a suit in OS.No.4534/2020 against the plaintiff seeking permanent injunction not to evict him from the suit property forcibly without following due process of law.
The suit schedule premises measures 11.14836 sq.mtrs, which is less than 14 sq.mtrs and it is a commercial premises, so this court has no jurisdiction to try this suit.
The plaintiff has received the rentals paid subsequent to issuance of notice and he is not due to pay any arrears of rent.
Hence, prays to dismiss the suit.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the then Presiding Officer as framed issues on 20.06.2022 and additional issues on 09.06.2023 as under:

On behalf of the defendant, he himself got examined as DW.1 and got marked exhibit D1 to D7.
6.
Heard learned counsel for both the parties.
Perused the materials on record.

The learned counsel for the defendant, during the course of argument drew the attention of this court to Ex.P1 sale deed of the plaintiff, wherein, in the schedule, total M V Jaikumar vs Sendil Kumar V G on 15 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194964507/

sentences.text: 9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the plaintiff argued that 160 sq.ft amounts to 14.86448 sq.mtrs and in Ex.P2 it is clearly mentioned that there are two floors, each measuring 11.14836 sq.mtrs, so this court has jurisdiction.
Of course, in Ex.P2, at the bottom, it is clearly mentioned that there are two floors, i.e. Ground and First floor, each measuring 11.14836 sq.mtrs.
Further, in the plaint schedule also, the plaintiff has described the tenanted shop premises, consisting of ground floor Judgment and first floor, measuring 320 sq.ft.

In fact, in para-5 of the written statement, the defendant has categorically admitted that during the pendency of the tenancy, he carried out repairs of the suit premises and built one more floor on top at his cost by spending Rs.2,50,000/-.

Thereby,
the defendant himself admits that there are two floors.

Even in the reply notice at Ex.P7 sent by the advocate for the defendant, in reply to the quit notice issued by the advocate for the plaintiff at para-2, he mentions that the plaintiff is the owner of the shop No.85 consisting of ground and first floor.

Even in the cross-examination of DW1, at page 10, when Ex.P10 photograph was confronted,
he admitted that he is carrying out the business in the premises which is having both ground floor with shutter and the first floor.

Thus, evidence on record could clearly show that suit schedule premises is consisting of ground and first floor and having measurement more than 22 sq.mtrs, so definitely it is more than 14 sq.mtrs, hence this court has got jurisdiction to try this suit.

Of course,
the learned counsel for the defendant has relied upon the decision of the Hon.ble High Court of Karnataka in K. Thimmegowda Vs. B.S. Nagaraj Rao and others, (ILR 2008 KAR 2753), wherein the Hon.ble High Court elaborately discussed what is 'plinth area' and 'carpet area' and held that in a suit for ejectment, the court has to consider the total plinth area and not carpet area.

sentences.text: As such, the above decision, in fact, not helpful to the defendant, but clarifies the fact that the total measurement of the leased out premises in favor of the defendant consisting of more than 22 sq.mtrs plinth area.

Hence the above issue is answered in the 'negative'.
Judgment 10. Issue No.1 & Addl. Issue No.1:-
Once jural relationship is admitted, the next question would be whether the tenancy has been legally terminated as required under law.
It is an admitted fact that the plaintiff issued legal notice at Ex.P4, Ex.P6 is postal acknowledgment card, Ex.P5 is the postal receipt.
The defendant issued reply notice at Ex.P7 and he sent a cheque dated 10.12.2020 for Rs.15,000/- towards rent.
For that, the plaintiff through his counsel issued a rejoinder dated 29.01.2021 at Ex.P8 and accepted that rent paid through cheque.
Ex.P9 is the postal receipt, Ex.P3 is the tax paid receipt.
11. In the instant case, though there is a lease agreement admitted by the parties, it is an unregistered lease agreement, so it is not marked before the court.
As admitted by the parties, the lease had commenced in the year 2014 and it continued even after 2017.

Hence, the tenancy can be M V Jaikumar vs Sendil Kumar V G on 15 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194964507/
4 terminated by issuing 15 days quit notice as required under Sec.106 of the Transfer of Property Act.

sentences.text: So, by issuing Ex.P7 quit notice, the plaintiff has lawfully terminated the tenancy of the defendant.

12. However, the learned counsel for the defendant would argue, though not pleaded in the written statement or no evidence is let in that, since the plaintiff has accepted the rent, even after issuance of the quit notice, it amounts to waiver of notice, so the tenancy is not validly terminated and the defendant is entitled to continue as a tenant of the premises.
This argument does not hold good for more than one reason.
As mentioned above, absolutely Judgment there is no pleading to that effect.
When there is no pleading, a party to a suit cannot lead evidence or argue something which is contrary to the pleading or not at all pleaded.
Secondly, merely the landlord accepted the rentals subsequent to issuance of the quit notice that will not automatically amounts to waiver of notice.
There shall be evidence to show that, the landlord intended to waive the notice and to treat the lease as subsisting.
In the case on hand, no such evidence is placed on record.
Hence the above contention of the defendant without any foundation has to be rejected in-limine.
13. The plaintiff has stated that the suit schedule premises is required for his personal use.
In the cross examination of DW.1 at page-10, he admitted that plaintiff has an adult son, who is unemployed.
It was suggested to DW.1 that the suit premises is required for plaintiff's son to carry out business therein, for that defendant said, he wants some time to vacate the premises.
In fact, he said so in his cross examination dated 04.12.2023.
That means, already more than 1 year 3 months has been elapsed from the date, he sought some time to vacate the premises.

For all these reasons,
this Court is of the considered view that the plaintiff has validly terminated the tenancy of the defendant by issuing quit notice as required under law, so the defendant is liable to deliver vacant possession of the suit schedule property in favour of the plaintiff.
Accordingly, above Issue No.1 and Addl. Issue No.1 are answered in the 'affirmative'.

Judgment 14. Issue No.2:-
The plaintiff in his plaint as well examination in chief affidavit has stated, as per the lease agreement dated 01.04.2017, the rent was fixed was Rs.15,000/- per month for 11 months.
Thereafter, the defendant was liable to pay Rs.16,500/- from 01.08.2018 and Rs.18,150/- from 01.07.2019 and from 01.06.2020 Rs.19,965/-.

As such, as on 30.10.2020, the defendant is liable to pay Rs.6,45,975/-, which after deduction of security deposit Rs.4 lakhs and subsequent payment of Rs.45,000, the defendant is liable to pay Rs.2,15,975 towards arrears of rent.
15. On the other hand, the defendant has denied his liability to pay arrears of rent or the rent calculated at enhanced rate by the plaintiff.
Admittedly, the lease agreement is not produced by the plaintiff and got it marked.
Though he says that the lease was for a period of 2 years under the agreement dated 01.04.2017, as admitted by the party, it is not a registered document.

Once it is proved that there is no registered lease agreement, as required under Sec.107 of TP Act, then parties to the said unregistered lease agreement cannot rely upon that except for collateral purposes.

An M V Jaikumar vs Sendil Kumar V G on 15 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194964507/
5 unregistered lease agreement cannot be looked into for the purpose of proving of term of lease or period of lease or rate of rent.

sentences.text: Therefore, the contention of the plaintiff with respect to the enhanced rate of rent once in 11 months and the calculation he made in the plaint are completely without any base, unilateral and it cannot be considered by the court.
Judgment 16.

In fact, DW.1 has produced registration certificate of his shop at Ex.D1 issued by BBMP for food safety, GST registration certificate at Ex.D2, income tax returns for the assessment year 2021-22 at Ex.D3, Electricity bills at Ex.D6.
Further he has produced, bank statement of his Indian Bank Account at Ex.D4 from 27.11.2020 to 05.11.2022, 9 rent receipts at Ex.D5.
4 Rent receipts at Ex.D8 & D9.

These rent receipts and bank statements would clearly show that the defendant has been paying rentals at Rs.15,000/- to the plaintiff continuously, even after filing of the suit and that was received by the plaintiff without any protest.
As per the said documents, the rent has been paid till October 2022.

Though the plaintiff has tried to deny this fact or not stated anything about the receipt of rentals from the defendant and though contended in his plaint and affidavit that the defendant is liable to pay arrears of rent even prior to the suit, the above documents go against his contention.
More particularly, DW.1 has produced a letter dated 05.03.2022 at Ex.D7 sent by the plaintiff to the defendant.
This letter is not denied by the plaintiff and it bears his signature.
The said letter which was issued subsequent to the suit and not denied by the plaintiff goes against the case of the plaintiff.

The relevant portions at para-1 & 7 of the said letter are reproduced for proper and better appreciation:
"1. I state that you has made upto date payment of rent due prior to the Cheques Payment by way of Cash to me, though the cheque bearing No.020937 dated 10.12.2020 of Allahabad Bank Tasker town Branch Bangalore was sent to me through RPAD duly acknowledged by my wife Mrs. J. Davi on 12.12.2020, I have encashed the payment.'

Judgment '7. Further to that there is no rent due from your side on account of payment of February, 2022 monthly rent due and there is no balance from your side on account of payment of February, 2022

, I request you to make payment of monthly rent as and when due as per English calendar month on or before 5th of succeeding month."
17.

In the said Ex.D7 letter, the plaintiff has admitted the payment of rentals by the defendant at different intervals and in fact in para-2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of Ex.D7, the plaintiff admitted payment of Rs.15,000/-, Rs.45,000/-, Rs.60,000/-, Rs.90,000/- and Rs.15,000 respectively.
Finally, he clearly says, there is no rent due from the defendant on account of payment of February 2022 monthly rent due and he requests to make monthly rentals in future.
So, from this letter, it is amply clear that the plaintiff admits the clearance of rent up to 2022.
In fact, from the bank statement produced at Ex.D4 as well the rent receipts Ex.D5, 8 & 9, not disputed by the plaintiff, it is clear that the defendant has paid rent up to the month October 2022.
Of course, there is no evidence placed by both the parties what has happened subsequent to that, that is from November 2022.
Anyhow, there are ample evidence to show up to October 2022, the defendant has paid the rentals.

Unfortunately,
the plaintiff who has come to the court seeking ejectment and recovery of arrears of rent has not M V Jaikumar vs Sendil Kumar V G on 15 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194964507/
6 come to the court with clean hands.

sentences.text: In spite of clear evidence placed on record by the defendant, the plaintiff has not made any attempt to submit to the court, the calculation of rent paid subsequent to the suit.
It amounts to suppression of material facts.
A party litigant is always expected to be true to the court by placing all material evidence.
The plaintiff is guilty of suppression Judgment of material facts from this court.
Anyhow, the evidence as discussed above would clearly show that the defendant has cleared the rent up to October 2022.
The plaintiff is still duty bound to file a payment chart regarding any payment towards the rent from November 2022 made by the defendant.
18. For all these reasons, this court is of the considered view that the plaintiff is not entitled for the relief of recovery of arrears of rent as prayed by him with interest.
However, the plaintiff is entitled for the rentals after November 2022, if not paid by the defendant till the date of the judgment.
Accordingly, the above issue is answered.
19. Issue No.3:-
The plaintiff has also sought for damages at the rate of Rs50,000/- per month from the date of the suit till the date of handing over vacant possession of the suit premises.

As discussed above, there are clear evidence to show that even during the pendency of the suit, the plaintiff has received rentals and sent a letter to the defendant stating that there is no due of payment of rent from the side of the defendant till October 2022.
Thereafter, the evidence shows that till the month of October 2022, the rentals were paid by the defendant.

In fact, in his cross examination PW.1, at page-2 clearly admitted, the defendant is paying Rs.15,000/-
rentals regularly and he did not issue receipt towards the rent paid by the defendant prior to filing of the suit in OS.No.4534/2020.
That shows, the plaintiff was not in the habit of issuing rent Judgment receipts earlier.
It is only subsequent to the filing of the injunction suit by the defendant, the plaintiff has started to issue rent receipts.
20. No doubt, a landlord after termination of the tenancy is entitled for damages.
However, he has to lead evidence to that effect.
In this suit, the plaintiff has not led any evidence to show that he is entitled for damages at the rate of Rs.50,000/- per month.

As already discussed on Issue No.2, since the rentals were paid even after filing the suit and during the pendency of the suit and the plaintiff has failed to provide proper account statement with regard to the rent paid by the defendant
, till the date of the judgment, the plaintiff is entitled to recover the rentals at Rs.15,000/- per month.

It is only after the judgment and decree, if there is any delay in handing over the vacant possession of the suit property, the plaintiff is entitled for damages for unauthorized occupation of the schedule premises.
In that event, the plaintiff is entitled to mesne-profit or damages.
In that respect, a separate inquiry may be conducted if the plaintiff wants to prosecute against the defendant.
Accordingly, the above issue is answered.

sentences.text: Judgment ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is decreed with costs.
The defendant is directed to quit and deliver vacant possession of the suit schedule property in favour of the plaintiff within one month from the date of this order.

The defendant shall pay the arrears of rent at the rate of Rs.15,000/- per month from November 2022 till the date of judgment after deducting any payment if made subsequently by filing a joint memo of calculation in the office.

If the defendant fails to deliver vacant possession within one month from the date of judgment, the plaintiff is at liberty to file a petition for separate inquiry for mesne profit under O.XX Rule 12 of CPC.
Draw Decree accordingly.
